overall: AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the Board did not meet on the alleged February 1 date, and minutes posting is not legally required, though the letter explained the city-calendar posting requirement and minutes timing rules as guidance.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board failed to properly post notice of a meeting held February 1; the AG found the Board did not meet that day.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Board did not meet on February 1, we find that the Board did not fail to properly post notice of this meeting, and therefore did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: AG noted Board meeting notices were posted only to the Board's own website, not the City's official calendar; explained the required posting location as guidance.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Board is considered a local public body and the City of Watertown has adopted its website as the official posting location for all public bodies within the municipality, the Board must post notice of its meetings to https://www.watertown-ma.gov/calendar.

allegations.summary: Complaint raised concern that the Board does not post its meeting minutes; the AG explained what the law requires for minutes.
allegations.key_passage: the Open Meeting Law does not require that public bodies post their minutes to a website or that minutes be submitted to the Town Clerk, but rather that meeting minutes be made available within 10 days of a request.
